processes.name: Strangers Gas Contract meter flow: deal or write-off approval requests
processes.description: Clem Cernosek emails Daren Farmer one message per HPL meter where flow is booked to the Strangers Gas Contract. Each asks for a deal extension, a new deal, or a printed and signed write-off approval, and Logistics (Bob Cotten) then moves the volumes to a write-off contract.
processes.stall_points: Each request is a hand-written near-identical email that needs a printed, signed, returned original. Replies are slow, e.g. the trader still had to renegotiate and Mark McCoy was chasing for an answer.
processes.automation: Generate these requests from the meter/Strangers Gas report and route a one-click approve, extend or new-deal response with the write-off contract move logged automatically.

has been moved from the Strangers Gas Contract to 012-41500-02-004 for write-off purposes.

processes.name: Meter flow without a deal: ask to extend or create deal
processes.description: Volume schedulers and analysts (Aimee Lannou, Mary Poorman, Karen Lindley, Mike Olsen) find flow at meters with no nomination or expired deal. They email Daren Farmer to extend the deal or create a new one, often for a few days only. The flow lands on stranger's gas or the UA4 variance list until someone acts.
processes.stall_points: Everything funnels through Daren Farmer, who replies by email. Requests sit until he extends the deal, and one meter was queried again days later because the deal expired on day 3.
processes.automation: Auto-detect meters with flow and no live deal at month end, and give the deal owner a one-click extend-or-create task with the meter history prefilled.

processes.name: Arthur Andersen monthly P&L and origination support requests
processes.description: Each month the Arthur Andersen auditor emails the West desk lead for P&L top pages by region and for deal tickets and confirmations on selected deals. Darron Giron does not produce them himself. He forwards the request to Chris Walker, Jason Wolfe, Carole Frank and others and then chases to confirm they responded.
processes.stall_points: The requester asks who to contact and Giron is out of town, so the request waits and is forwarded several times. The auditor asks again within hours.
processes.automation: Keep a standing owner map of desks to P&L preparers. Auto-route auditor requests to the right owner and track completion, with top pages pulled from the P&L system.

evidence.quote: We are requesting that you supply the P & L top pages for the last day of the month for those regions that are applicable to you.

Please contact Mark and provide him with the documentation he needs.  Thanks.

processes.name: Deal rate, counterparty and booking corrections in Sitara/TAGG
processes.description: Back-office and risk colleagues email Darron Giron to change a rate, rebook a counterparty, update pricing or confirm deal details on specific deals. He makes the change by hand and replies with a one-line confirmation. Some of these arrive monthly for the same deal.
processes.stall_points: Requests need a reminder before action, such as the Enervest rate change that took two weeks. The same deal is corrected every month.
processes.automation: Drive the recurring rate update from the monthly price source instead of by email. Give one change-request queue with status for rebooks and rate edits.

processes.name: Daily origination reporting and book/TDS mapping upkeep for the risk desks
processes.description: Giron forwards instructions from management to his risk team. They cover origination schedule entries for a daily report, new TDS desk and book setup, region-to-book mappings, and deals to flip to a new book. The team then updates the schedules and books manually.
processes.stall_points: Every instruction is relayed by forwarded email and depends on each recipient. Mistakes surface later, such as deals unwound in TAGG but not in Sitara.
processes.automation: Validate the required origination fields at entry. Reconcile TAGG and Sitara deal status automatically and keep book mappings in one maintained table.

processes.name: Analyst recruiting, rotation and interview scheduling
processes.description: Giron coordinates with HR (Andrea Richards, Toni Graham, Molly Magee) on analyst rotations and candidate interviews. He sends location, cost center and supervisor details by email, names interviewers and negotiates headcount with peer managers.
processes.stall_points: HR asks again for the same fields (location, department, cost center). Interview calendars need a separate assistant, and candidates chase HR.
processes.automation: Use a request form that captures analyst placement fields once. Add a shared interview scheduler for the panel.

processes.name: Weekend on-call notes distribution
processes.description: Logistics staff write up what happened during their weekend on call (calls from gas control, nomination and confirmation issues, deal ticket fixes). They email the notes or an attachment to the whole scheduling team on Monday.
processes.stall_points: Notes are written manually as narrative and sent to a long distribution list. Some arrive as attachments with no body text.
processes.automation: Use a structured on-call log that auto-publishes a weekly summary to the team.

evidence.quote: Please see the attached file for On-Call Notes.

processes.name: Customer and pipeline nomination changes and confirmations
processes.description: Nominations and nomination changes arrive by email and spreadsheet from customers, TXU and pipelines (Valero monthly nominations, Rohm & Haas, HPL daily nom file). Schedulers re-key them into deal tickets and check with Daren Farmer. A shared HPL.Scheduling mailbox was set up to centralize them.
processes.stall_points: Changes are re-keyed by hand from attachments and approved by email. Before the shared mailbox, a nomination change could be missed when an individual was out.
processes.automation: Ingest nomination spreadsheets automatically into deal tickets and flag differences from the current ticket. Alert on pipeline maintenance windows.
